test: 17-Step Admin CMS Persistence & PostgreSQL Authority Audit

steps.description: Open Admin CMS dashboard at http://localhost:3000/dashboard?tab=cms
Confirm Homepage (cmspg_home) is selected in Page Builder
Selected Page Title
Change subheading field to: "Fresh Artisan Patisserie Delivered Daily [Verified 16:22:04]"
Click Save Draft button
Confirm API response for Save Draft
Query PostgreSQL directly in read-only mode: SELECT id, title, slug, status, blocks, updated_at FROM cms_page WHERE id = 'cmspg_home'
Confirm exact changed value in PostgreSQL: "Fresh Artisan Patisserie Delivered Daily [Verified 16:22:04]" (matches: true)
Reload the admin browser page
Confirm reloaded value in input from API: "Fresh Artisan Patisserie Delivered Daily [Verified 16:22:04]" (matches: true)
Click Publish button and wait for publish API
Confirm published database row/version in PostgreSQL
PostgreSQL Published State
Open public homepage in a clean customer browser session (http://localhost:3000)
Confirm storefront rendering: HTTP 200, textPresent=true
Refresh public storefront page and confirm consistency
Storefront consistent after refresh: HTTP 200, textPresent=true
Perform process restart persistence check (verifying PostgreSQL durability independently of Node runtime memory)
Confirm exact value still exists in PostgreSQL after cold query
Restore original subheading through normal CMS flow: "Fresh Artisan Patisserie Delivered Daily [Verified 02:34:04]"
Original value restored in PostgreSQL
